core.title: Declare behaviour in hypermedia markup with the framework's declarative attributes, not inline event handlers
core.given: A non-test file of any kind carries at least one of the markup framework's declarative attributes (the stack's hypermedia markup marker); it is hypermedia-driven markup
core.when: You add or change element behaviour in that file
core.then: Use no inline event-handler attribute in that markup; declare the behaviour with the markup framework's declarative behaviour attributes instead
prefer: Declare behaviour that accompanies a declarative request on the framework's declarative behaviour attribute for that event, not on an inline handler of the same element (which is destroyed when the element is replaced).

The framework's element-scoped declarative attribute for element behaviour, its request-triggering attribute for the request itself; both survive content replacement because the framework re-processes new content.
Genuinely presentational, non-request behaviour: a delegated listener on a stable ancestor element that is never replaced.
avoid: Any inline event-handler attribute (the profile's inline event-handler form) in hypermedia-driven markup.
Mixing the two models: each inline handler is behaviour invisible to the markup framework's lifecycle; they accumulate and drift the codebase back toward a separate client-script layer.
unless: The file carries none of the framework's declarative attributes (self-scoping; never checked).
Event bindings of a different mechanism (the profile's component event props, not markup attributes): out of scope; only those bindings are exempt, not the files that contain them.
core.why: Replacing an element destroys its inline handler and any closed-over state; conversely a replaced-out element's handler can stay live on a detached node, firing stale events against markup the user can no longer see. The framework's declarative behaviour attributes participate in the framework's event and content-replacement lifecycle.
evidence: The markup convention check reports no inline event-handler attribute in any non-test file carrying the stack's hypermedia markup marker.
Reviewer confirms behaviour previously in inline handlers is expressed through the framework's declarative behaviour attributes, or a delegated listener on a stable ancestor that is never replaced.
verification: Content-based, self-scoping check with no file-kind or extension gate: step 1, confirm the file carries the stack's hypermedia markup marker, otherwise skip the file entirely; step 2, flag every inline event-handler attribute of the profile's forbidden form in it.

The check matches only the forbidden inline form, so handler-like bindings of a different mechanism (the profile's component event props) are never flagged, while a genuine inline handler inside a file that carries the marker IS flagged; the exemption covers only those bindings, not whole files.
Test files are excluded from the check; which files count as test files comes from the stack's role-independent test-file name patterns.
Severity 3; strict disposition: every finding fails the check, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: the edited file contains at least one of the markup framework's declarative attributes (hypermedia-driven markup)
the edited file is not a test file

fires: Editing any non-test hypermedia-driven markup file, even one that currently has no inline handlers (preventative guidance before one is introduced)
Editing markup that carries one of the framework's declarative request attributes and adding an inline event-handler attribute to that element
A file carrying the framework's declarative attributes also contains an inline event-handler attribute on any element
A component-template file that carries the framework's declarative attributes and also a genuine inline event-handler attribute (not an exempt component event prop)
doesNotFire: Markup with none of the framework's declarative attributes that uses an inline event-handler attribute

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself ('behaviour is declared where the markup framework can see it') is neutral, but four concrete forms had no home in the closed vocabulary and are proposed as idiom keys: the self-scoping declarative-attribute marker, the declarative behaviour constructs, the forbidden inline-handler form with its case rule, and the exempt component event-prop syntax. The test exclusion also needed a new proposed key: suffix.test, a role-independent test-file classification, because suffix.unit_test / suffix.acceptance_test / suffix.e2e_test each name one test role while Bun's `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` exclusion applies to test files of any role. The core keeps the check content-based with no file-kind gate, exactly matching the Bun semantics, so idiom.markup_kinds is deliberately unused (a kind gate would weaken or strengthen the obligation depending on the stack's kind list). The htmx code example, the detector/validator id and the rule terms stay in the Bun realization; severity '3' is kept in core:verification as instructed, though the numeric scale itself belongs to the realizing rule set. Bun's activation fact 'path_glob' was re-expressed as the allowed 'file_kind' fact, since the neutral fact vocabulary has no path_glob kind.
